claude_take: Two Chinese AI labs took opposite bets on the same day: Alibaba locked up Qwen4-Max's weights to chase enterprise revenue, while MiniMax gave away a comparably sharp 4K image model for free, and that split says more about where AI competition is heading than either release alone. Meanwhile Hollywood's two biggest stories both leaned on things no model can generate: a recognizable face taking over a 63-year-old franchise, and a director's leverage built on practical, in-camera spectacle rather than anything synthetic. Add a ground stop that froze the country's physical infrastructure and a mid-tier sneaker brand quietly out-growing the luxury giants by staying affordable, and the week's real theme isn't AI's advance so much as how much is still won by the specific, the tangible and the well-run.

items.headline: Alibaba Takes Qwen4-Max From Preview to General Availability
items.summary: Alibaba moved its flagship Qwen4-Max model out of preview and into general release, cutting API pricing and extending its context window to 1 million tokens while retiring the preview endpoint on November 25. Unlike most of Alibaba's recent Qwen releases, Qwen4-Max ships closed-weight, a shift the company frames around efficiency and agentic coding rather than openness. It is a meaningful update on the preview covered here last week, not a repeat of it.

items.headline: MiniMax Open-Sources H3-Image, a 4K Image Model
items.summary: MiniMax released H3-Image as an open-weight model capable of generating native 4K images in under ten seconds, with support for text-to-image, reference-based generation and editing using up to 16 reference images. The company published the weights on Hugging Face rather than keeping the model proprietary, a notable contrast with rivals racing to lock up their best image and video models behind paid APIs.

items.headline: Robert Pattinson Officially Cast as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's Reboot
items.summary: Amazon MGM Studios confirmed Robert Pattinson as the seventh actor to play James Bond, in a reboot directed by Denis Villeneuve from a script by Steven Knight, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing. Pattinson, who is only the third Englishman cast as Bond after Daniel Craig and Roger Moore, called the role a dream come true; no release date or supporting cast has been announced yet.

items.headline: Christopher Nolan's Universal Deal Looks Shrewder as 'The Odyssey' Keeps Breaking Records
items.summary: New reporting on Christopher Nolan's move to Universal after his split from Warner Bros. argues the studio's willingness to let him keep reaping profit from 'The Odyssey' early in its theatrical run, rather than waiting for the film to turn a profit on paper, has made him Hollywood's most sought-after director. Warner Bros., by contrast, reportedly never mounted a serious bid to win him back.

items.headline: Supreme Court Declines to Revive Trump Administration's DEI-Linked Grant Cuts
items.summary: The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's appeal in a case over roughly $59 million in federal research grants canceled at the University of California, leaving in place an appeals court ruling that found the cancellations likely violated the First Amendment. The justices gave no explanation and recorded no dissents; coverage noted the court separately declined to hear other administration appeals tied to diversity, equity and inclusion disputes.

items.headline: Historic Nationwide Ground Stop Exposed How Fragile US Air Travel Still Is
items.summary: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop after intermittent telecommunications outages, halting departures for more than four hours in what several outlets called the longest such stoppage since the September 11 attacks. Thousands of flights were still delayed or canceled the following day as airlines worked through the backlog, underscoring how a single technical fault can still cascade through the entire US air system.

items.headline: Golden Goose Keeps Growing While Luxury's Biggest Names Stall
items.summary: Golden Goose reported 16% revenue growth for the first nine months of 2026, reaching €583.3 million, with direct-to-consumer sales up 21% and wholesale returning to growth. The Italian sneaker brand's run stands out against a backdrop of slowing demand at Hermès, Kering and other major houses, suggesting accessible luxury is weathering the current slowdown better than the ultra-high end.

items.headline: Study Finds a Distinct Breathing Pattern Linked to ADHD
items.summary: Research presented at the Society for Neuroscience's Neuroscience 2026 meeting found that young adults with ADHD show a breathing pattern that differs from people without the condition, and that the pattern shifts when they take stimulant medication. The finding, from a Weizmann Institute of Science team, adds a physiological marker to a condition usually assessed through behavior alone.

items.headline: Plato's Allegory of the Cave
items.headline_fr: L'allégorie de la caverne de Platon
items.summary: In Book VII of 'The Republic,' Plato describes prisoners chained in a cave since birth, watching shadows cast on a wall and mistaking them for reality, until one is freed, sees the world outside, and struggles to convince the others of what he has seen. The allegory argues that most of what we take for knowledge is shadow and opinion, and that real understanding requires a difficult turn toward first principles, education and reasoned inquiry. It remains one of philosophy's sharpest images for the gap between appearance and reality, as relevant to algorithmic feeds and manufactured realism as it was to Athenian politics.
items.summary_fr: Au livre VII de « La République », Platon décrit des prisonniers enchaînés dans une caverne depuis leur naissance, regardant des ombres projetées sur un mur et les prenant pour la réalité, jusqu'à ce que l'un d'eux soit libéré, découvre le monde extérieur et peine à convaincre les autres de ce qu'il a vu. L'allégorie soutient que l'essentiel de ce que nous tenons pour savoir n'est qu'ombre et opinion, et qu'une véritable compréhension exige un effort difficile vers les principes premiers, l'éducation et la réflexion rationnelle. Elle reste l'une des images les plus frappantes de la philosophie sur l'écart entre apparence et réalité, tout aussi pertinente face aux flux algorithmiques et au réalisme fabriqué qu'elle l'était pour la politique athénienne.
